page: Microsoft Azure E32-8ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features a constrained CPU architecture with 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores and 8 threads, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration through AES and VAES.

Hardware allocation is heavily weighted toward memory density, providing 256.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 32.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Storage architecture includes a bundled 1288 GB local SSD drive alongside support for Azure Premium Storage, with no integrated discrete GPUs present. Memory subsystem benchmarks show a cached read bandwidth of 417.04 GB/sec and an uncached large-block read speed of 59.66 GB/sec with 43.37 GB/sec write throughput.

Synthetic compute benchmarks place the instance within the mid-tier performance distribution, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 1681.0, a multi-core score of 6221.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 11487.3. Database and caching workloads register solid results, achieving 7.97 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and a PassMark database rating of 4096.32. Compute-bound tasks with larger footprint models expose processing limitations, as medium 7B LLM inference yields only 7.57 tokens per second during generation.

The constrained CPU count lowers software licensing fees for products metered per core while maintaining the large memory footprint and high I/O throughput of an otherwise 32-core chassis. This operational profile fits relational database management systems, in-memory caches, enterprise data warehousing, and intensive ETL pipelines that require massive memory capacities without scaling up compute licensing overhead.

Driven by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores alongside 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding an expansive 32.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is bundled with a 1288 GB SSD, complemented by support for Azure Premium Storage, while discrete GPUs are omitted. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate solid memory bandwidth reaching 59.66 GB/sec for uncached reads, robust throughput of 7.97 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 6221.0. This configuration serves memory-bound architectures, including relational databases, high-capacity caching instances, and data analytics pipelines where database software licensing costs are linked directly to active core counts.
